DAXX uses two small hydrophobic residues to distinguish H3.3 from H3.2.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of histone variant specificity by DAXX, a chaperone protein involved in chromatin maintenance.
the structural and functional characterization of the DAXX–H3.3– H4 complex, which may be important for the understanding of the mechanisms of histone chaperones in chromatin assembly.
the structure and function of a histone variant, H3.3.

DAXX uses the hydrophobic pocket and polar environment to distinguish H3.3 from H3.2 and H3.1.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DAXX–H3.3–DAXX–H4 complex is a structural and functional unit that is required for proper chromatin organization in mammals.
the DAXX chaperone recognizes the H3.3 histone variant through a hydrophobic pocket that is formed by residues in both the histone-binding and histone-fold domains.
DAXX is able to recognize the H3.3 variant by a combination of hydrophobic and polar interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the histone chaperones can distinguish between the canonical and variant histones with high precision and that this specificity is mediated by the histone variants themselves.
